Research dossier: FN — Fabrinet

Researched: 2026-07-11 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.68 · Opportunity score: 71

Next earnings: 2026-08-24

Business

Thailand-based precision contract manufacturer of optical and electro-mechanical packages — the

company that physically assembles and tests high-speed optical transceivers (800G now, 1.6T

ramping) and related photonics for other people's brands. Customers are the optical/networking

primes and, increasingly, the chip vendor itself: NVIDIA (~30% of revenue, sell-side sees up to

~50% annualized), plus Cisco, Coherent, Lumentum, Ciena, and a named direct hyperscaler

relationship (AWS, plus two newer direct datacom programs ramping through FY27). FN reportedly

holds a majority-to-~100% share on the 1.6T transceivers feeding NVIDIA's Blackwell platform

(one March 2026 Barclays note flagged "great uncertainty" on Blackwell 1.6T timing, but that call

is now four months stale and has been superseded by two subsequent Barclays PT raises — $537

in Jan → $702 in May — i.e. Barclays itself walked the caution back). Revenue durably continues

because FN owns scarce precision-manufacturing capacity and yield/quality entrenchment primes

don't want to rebuild — they design the optics, FN builds them. It is a **substrate /

picks-and-shovels** play in the orchestration-vs-substrate frame: real earnings, but thin

(~10% net) contract-manufacturing margins and limited IP/pricing power. Unchanged since the last

dive.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

The business is unchanged; the price has kept falling, and it did so exactly on the schedule the

6/27 and 7/4 dossiers pre-committed to. Since the 7/4 dive (BUY at $499.61, add-toward-lower-end),

FN has taken a third leg down: last close $471.13-$471.16 (screen 7/11), off 36.9%

from the 52-week high (was 33.0% on 7/4), -9.8% vs the 200DMA (was -3.7% — the break below

trend has deepened, not reversed), ret_60d -30.9%. The 7/4 dossier explicitly wrote: *"A

third cohort-wide leg to ~$470 with the group still moving together → add again, same thesis,

better price."* That is precisely what happened, and the cohort-confirmation test still passes:

AAOI/COHR/LITE fell again together (AAOI -17% to $114.93, COHR -10% to $331.57, LITE -10% to

$720.91 around 7/1-7/2), and a broader semiconductor selloff hit July 6-7 after Samsung's Q2

print — a 19x profit beat that still triggered an 8% Samsung drop and a >$1.3T sector-wide

semi wipeout (SOX -7-10% since 6/22) because DRAM pricing came in softer than the market's

extrapolated-forever assumption. That catalyst is about memory pricing, one step further

removed from FN's actual product (optics assembly, not DRAM) than the prior two legs, which were

at least inside the optics cohort itself. No FN-specific news surfaced in this window: no new

downgrade, no guidance change, no confirmed customer-share loss. Per macro-cohort-confirmation,

a third macro/cohort-wide leg with zero idiosyncratic news is still liquidity, not information.

**BUY, add — this is the third pre-committed add point, not a fresh idea, and the discount is now

deeper than either prior entry.**

Valuation + position vs. range

  • Price ~$471 ($471.13 stockanalysis 7/10 close, $471.16 screen); market cap $16.88B;

52-wk range $272.49–$748.89 (off-high 36.9%, +72.2% above the low). ret_20d -18.8%,

ret_60d -30.9%, -24.2% vs 50DMA, -9.8% vs 200DMA — now solidly, not marginally,

below the 200-day trend line.

  • Trailing P/E 40.47, forward P/E 28.75 (down from 30.49 three weeks ago, down from 32.0

five weeks ago — a straight-line multiple compression across three legs with the same TTM

fundamentals). Revenue TTM $4.24B (+29.8%); net income TTM $420.97M (+29.0%); EPS TTM

$11.64; ~35.83M shares. Implied NTM EPS ~$16.4 (471.13 / 28.75), essentially

unchanged from the last two dives — the multiple moved, not the earnings estimate.

  • My fair-value read, unchanged methodology: 30–35× forward on a ~30%-grower with

single-customer concentration and a CPO hedge (Raytek) → $492–$574. At ~$471 the market now

pays 28.75× NTM — below the floor of that band for the first time across three dives (was

bottom-of-band at 30.5× on 7/4, mid-band at 32.0× on 6/27). Sell-side average 12-mo PT sits at

Post-deal / repriced check

Not a Wait-for-deal thesis name, but the repriced discipline applies and has now moved a

third increment in the buyer's favor: the de-rate that "fully opened" at $525 on 6/27 and reached

the "bottom of the band" at $500 on 7/4 has now **broken through the bottom of the fair band

entirely** at $471, still with no fundamentally new negative FN-specific information. Three

consecutive cohort/macro legs down is the point where the falsification note from 7/4 said the

"structural repricing vs. dip" question needs to be taken seriously rather than dismissed — this

dive treats it seriously by (a) confirming the newest leg's catalyst (Samsung DRAM miss) is

memory-specific and one degree further from FN's actual optics-assembly business than the prior

legs, and (b) confirming credit markets are still not reacting (macro.md: BBB ~100bp, HY

~267-285bp, unmoved through the entire window including the Iran/oil episode). Two independent

non-FN, non-optics catalysts (Meta Compute report, Samsung DRAM miss) producing three legs of the

same cohort de-rate is unusual, but it is still a multiple story, not an FN earnings story —

nothing in this window contradicts FN's own Q3 FY26 print (+39% YoY, telecom record $628.3M) or

the 1.6T Blackwell ramp.

Council (one line each, no hedging)

  • Bull: Sole-scale assembler of the exact 1.6T optics the AI buildout needs, +39% and

accelerating, now three cohort/macro legs into a de-rate that has pushed the multiple through

the bottom of a reasonable 30-35× band to 28.75× with zero FN-specific bad news across any of

the three legs and Street targets unchanged ~59% above spot — this is the best absolute price

either of the two prior dives got.

  • Bear: Three consecutive legs down in five weeks, each blamed on "someone else's" news

(cohort valuation, Meta Compute, Samsung DRAM), is exactly the pattern a genuine regime change

looks like in real time before anyone admits it — a ~10%-margin contract manufacturer with

30-50% revenue concentration on one customer does not deserve the benefit of the doubt

indefinitely, and "it's not about us" narrated three times in a row is what a broken chart

sounds like from the inside.

  • First-principles: A capacity-and-yield business with no IP moat and one dominant customer

is worth ~30-35× only while the pluggable cycle and that customer's volume hold; at 28.75× fwd

with +30% growth, three cohort/macro-confirmed legs, and still no fundamental deterioration in

FN's own numbers, the price now pays more margin of safety than fair for the concentration

risk — but the falsification bar (a fourth leg, or any FN-specific negative) is closer than it

was three weeks ago simply because less room remains before "structural reset" has to be taken

literally rather than provisionally.

Macro fit

Falsification

  • 30-day: A fourth cohort/macro-wide leg to ~$450 with the group still moving together →

add again, same thesis, better price, but flag explicitly that four legs is the point to

reweight toward "structural" over "dip." A bounce back above ~$525-540 with no new catalyst →

stop adding, edge re-consumed. Any FN-specific bad news (a real NVIDIA-share loss, a margin

warning, a CPO-bypass confirmation, an idiosyncratic downgrade not tied to the broader cohort)

at any price → reassess to HOLD/AVOID immediately, not add.

  • 60-day (Aug 24 print): Q4 FY26 must confirm the 1.6T ramp, the two direct-hyperscaler

programs actually shipping revenue, and hold/expand the ~10% margin. A guide-down, margin

compression, or softening NVIDIA-share commentary → AVOID regardless of price. This print is

  • 90-day: A concrete CPO adoption signal that bypasses FN (a hyperscaler/NVIDIA CPO switch

deployment whose optical engines FN — including via Raytek — does not build) remains the

SemiAnalysis report arguing CPO mass production is delayed to 2028-2029 (yield/serviceability

NVDABUYfetched62›

Research dossier: NVDA — NVIDIA Corp

Researched: 2026-06-27 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.62 · Opportunity score: 62

Next earnings: 2026-08-26

Business

NVIDIA sells the accelerated-compute substrate for AI: data-center GPUs (Blackwell B200/B300,

Rubin ramping), the networking that lashes them into clusters (InfiniBand, Spectrum-X, NVLink),

and the CUDA software moat that keeps the ecosystem sticky. Customers are the hyperscalers

(~50% of Data Center revenue), plus a widening tail of AI clouds, sovereigns, enterprise and

industrial. Per Nvidia - AI Cycle Durability and GPU Economics, durability is the only

question that matters for the valuation, and it rests on two legs: (a) hyperscaler capex

continuing to ramp, and (b) GPU economics — rental price and useful life — staying firm. Both

are still standing, but both took a knock this month (see below).

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

Qualified yes, but lower-conviction than two weeks ago. The fundamental floor is intact and the

valuation is the most attractive it's been: Q1 FY27 (2026-05-20) was a real acceleration —

revenue $81.6B (+85% YoY), Data Center a record $75.2B (+92%), and Q2 guided to $91B

(~+11% sequential), paired with an $80B buyback and a 25× dividend raise. China H20 is already

zeroed from the run-rate (pure upside optionality). None of that has broken.

What changed since the 2026-06-13 dossier, and why I'm marking down:

  • The catalyst went stale. The May-20 print is now 5+ weeks old. The macro discipline

(extended-with-vs-without-catalyst) wants a real dip OR a fresh catalyst. We now have

the dip but no fresh catalyst — the new news flow is net-negative (below), and the next

thesis event is the Aug-26 print, two months out. A stale-catalyst dip is the weaker of the

two BUY conditions.

  • NVDA is the laggard, not the leader. It's the worst-performing major semi YTD (~+3.65%)

while the SOX is ~+70%, Micron ~+284%, AMD ~+138%. Capital rotated into memory/HBM and ASIC

beneficiaries. That underperformance is itself the opportunity-cost case (cheapest, highest

quality, de-rated) — but it also tells you the market is actively re-pricing NVDA's share of

the AI dollar downward, which is a signal, not just noise.

  • The ASIC share-shift is now visible in the guide. Custom silicon is ~28% of 2026

hyperscaler capex (~$185B, up from <$30B in 2022); TrendForce sees custom-chip sales +45% in

2026 vs GPU shipments +16%. NVDA's own FY27 outlook bakes in ~18% growth (vs 112% FY26). The

Nvidia - AI Cycle Durability essay's counter still holds — GPUs win on useful-life/financing

vs single-purpose ASICs, and custom growing off a tiny base doesn't shrink NVDA's pie — but the

durability question now has a real, market-visible data point against it, which the prior

dossier underweighted.

  • GPU cloud-rental is softening (kill-switch #2 yellow flag, NOT tripped — see Macro fit).

So: a genuine value setup in the single best AI franchise, on a real ~18% pullback to its

200-DMA — but bought into a hawkish-Fed/extended-market tape with a stale catalyst and a growing

(if overstated) ASIC overhang. That's a BUY you stage and trigger-gate, not one you chase at

market. Dip-buyer base rate supports the setup but demands humility: **33 instances, 67.7% win

at +21/42/63d, avg +12.4% at +63d, but worst-case -45.2% and avg max drawdown -11.8%.**

Valuation + position vs. range

Price $192.53 (close 2026-06-26); market cap $4.66T; **trailing P/E 29.5, forward P/E

19.4 (fetched, stockanalysis.com); TTM revenue $253.5B (+70.7%), net income $159.6B

(+108%), 24.22B shares. Implied forward EPS ≈ $9.94. Screen: 18.8% off the 52-wk high**

(ATH $235.47 on 2026-05-14), +26.7% above the low, sitting right on its 200-DMA

(+0.7%) and -8.6% below the 50-DMA — mid-range, decidedly not extended.

The standout fact persists and has gotten stronger: the single largest AI beneficiary trades

at a forward multiple (~19.4×) BELOW the S&P 500 itself (~20–22×) — cheaper than the 20.7×

in the 6/13 read — while growing revenue 70%+ and earnings 100%+. My fair-value read: a clean,

cash-generative, buyback-supported grower of this quality earns more than a market multiple even

after haircutting for the ASIC share-shift. At a conservative 22× forward EPS that's ~$219; the

market is paying ~19.4×, pricing in a deceleration sharper than the Q2 guide shows. **Much is

priced in on growth; the multiple is now pricing in active share-loss — that gap is the edge,

but it's a thinner edge than before because the share-loss concern is real, not imagined.**

Post-deal / repriced check

Wait-for-deal thesis doesn't apply cleanly — NVDA is the substrate collecting the capex,

not a small provider waiting on one lab's offtake to reprice it; there's no single deal whose

announcement consumed the entry edge. On the ai-capex-payback-window J-curve, NVDA is on the

right side: it books the cash now (positive FCF, fortress balance sheet); the FCF compression

is the customers' problem. The relevant repricing here is the multiple — and it has moved the

right way for a buyer (compressed to a sub-market 19.4× forward), which is what makes this an

entry candidate rather than a chase. The thesis break would be kill-switch #1 (customers cutting

capex) — not visible; capex still +77% YoY and being raised.

Council (one line each, no hedging)

  • Bull: The best AI franchise on earth, a 100%-earnings-grower with a CUDA moat and an $80B

buyback, trading at a below-market forward multiple after an 18% pullback to its 200-DMA —

the cohort laggard, not the leader.

  • Bear: The AI dollar is visibly migrating to custom silicon (~28% of capex, +45% growth),

cloud-rental is rolling over, insiders dumped $410M in 3 months, and the FY27 guide already

concedes 18% growth — the durability question is being answered the wrong way in real time.

  • First-principles: At 19× forward earnings of a business compounding 70%+ with the world

still short watts and wafers through 2027, you're underpaying for the durability — unless

ASICs structurally cap NVDA's share, in which case 19× is a value trap on a decelerating peak.

Synopsys is one half of the EDA (electronic design automation) duopoly with Cadence — the

build. The July-2025 Ansys acquisition bolted on multi-physics simulation (structural / thermal /

fluids / electromagnetics), extending the franchise from "design the chip" toward "simulate the

whole system" (the new Multiphysics Fusion product line, launched June 2026, is the first

integrated output). Customers are every fabless designer, IDM, foundry, and increasingly the

hyperscalers building custom AI silicon. Revenue durably continues because EDA is mission-critical,

deeply embedded in customer workflows, multi-year-licensed, and carries enormous switching costs —

you do not re-tool a $100M tape-out mid-flight. This is the **deepest picks-and-shovels layer of

through SNPS/CDNS tools before it exists in silicon. A structural workflow moat — not a temporal

wait-for-deal scarcity play.

Research dossier: CCJ — Cameco Corporation

Researched: 2026-07-04 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.58 · Opportunity score: 58

Business

Cameco is the largest publicly traded Western uranium producer, mining the highest-grade

deposits on Earth (Athabasca Basin: McArthur River/Key Lake, Cigar Lake). Three legs:

(1) uranium — production sold mostly under multi-year, market-related utility contracts;

(2) fuel services — UF6/UO2 conversion and CANDU fuel bundles; (3) Westinghouse — its

49% stake (Brookfield 51%) in the reactor-technology business: AP1000 new-build, fuel

fabrication, and reactor servicing. Revenue durability is high: nuclear is must-run baseload,

fuel demand is inelastic once a plant is committed, and utilities contract years forward.

FY2026 guidance reaffirmed at Q1: 29–32M lbs uranium delivered (19.5–21.0M lbs production +

up to 3M lbs market purchases), unchanged as of the last update. New this run: on **July 2,

2026 Cameco closed the acquisition of TEPCO Resources' 5% Cigar Lake JV interest** (~$115.75M),

lifting its Cigar Lake stake 2.87pp to 57.418% (Orano to 42.582%) — a bolt-on that increases

Cameco's leverage to its own highest-grade asset.

The June-27 dossier flagged CCJ as a HOLD sitting "at the top of the buy-below-to-fair zone,"

return -15.8%.

The drivers of the fall are name-specific, not macro contagion, and on inspection they are

not thesis damage: (1) a temporary Cigar Lake suspension (announced ~Jul 1) after

Research dossier: FSLR — First Solar

Researched: 2026-07-11 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.55 · Opportunity score: 55

Next earnings: 2026-07-23

Business

First Solar is the largest US-domiciled solar module maker, building thin-film cadmium-telluride (CdTe) panels rather than the polysilicon modules that dominate globally — a technology that structurally sidesteps the silicon trade war and the pending Section 232 polysilicon case. Revenue is ~96% US, from domestic fabs in Ohio, Alabama, and Louisiana plus older Malaysia/Vietnam capacity now running at deliberately low utilization (~20%) to avoid reciprocal tariffs. Customers are utility-scale developers and corporate clean-energy buyers on multi-year, fixed-price, take-or-pay contracts. The P&L rides two US policy levers: (1) Section 45X manufacturing credits (~$0.17/W thin-film; FY26 EBITDA guide $2.6–2.8B is still credit-heavy), sold for cash (>$2.0B transferred to date); (2) tariffs (Section 201 expired Feb 2026; 301/AD-CVD plus a pending Section 232 polysilicon case) that wall off Chinese/SE-Asian supply. Demand durability is real (contracted backlog + AI-driven electricity growth); the risk is concentrated in policy and litigation overhang, not end-demand.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

This is the third dossier on this name in three weeks (6/25 HOLD → 7/3 BUY → today), so the job tonight is mostly stress-testing the 7/3 BUY call rather than re-deriving from scratch. The 7/3 dive flipped to BUY on a real dip (price through both DMAs, −29.9% off high) plus a still-unfired Section 232 catalyst, sized small against a lawsuit + insider-selling overhang. Eight trading days later:

1. Price has round-tripped sideways, not resolved either way. $224.57 (7/2) → $227.71–227.83 (7/10 close, per screen and stockanalysis). Off-52w-high has actually widened slightly to 28.9% (52w high itself likely ticked, or rounding), still below both the 50dma (vs_50dma −8.3%) and closer to the 200dma (vs_200dma −3.3%, materially tighter than the 7/3 read's −8.3%/−4.4% split — the 200dma has been drifting down toward spot). Net: still squarely in the dip_buyer entry shape, not yet reverted.

2. The Section 232 catalyst did NOT resolve on the 7/4 date the 7/3 dossier flagged — it's now firmly dated to early August. Roth Capital Partners (via pv-magazine-usa, 6/22, and corroborated in this week's Wells Fargo note) has the White House proclamation slipping from late-June/early-July expectations to early August 2026. This is a delay, not a cancellation, and sell-side has gotten more bullish on the outcome in the interim, not less (see below) — but it means the binary the prior dossier expected "any day" is now confirmed to land roughly 3-4 weeks out, likely straddling the 7/23 Q2 print.

3. Sell-side has moved decisively bullish since 7/3, which the 7/3 dossier didn't have. Wells Fargo raised FSLR to $320 PT from $255 (7/6, "asymmetric upside" framing on the Section 232 outcome) and Deutsche Bank upgraded to Buy from Neutral with a $272 PT (7/7). Consensus PT has ticked up to $251.26 (from $247.30) even as spot barely moved — two fresh, dated, catalyst-specific upgrades from desks explicitly modeling the CdTe-favorable Section 232 scenario is a real (if lagging, sell-side-driven) confirmation of the 7/3 thesis, not new information the market has already priced — spot is flat since the upgrades.

The 7/7 resolved-thread finding (already in this pipeline's ledger) established the 135-sells/0-buys pattern was a routine 10b5-1 plan adopted 8 months before either catalyst went live — not a front-run signal. 6. The 2023 precedent is worth citing for the first time: First Solar previously won full dismissal-with-prejudice of an earlier securities class action (Series 6 cost-per-watt claims, dismissed June 2023). Different facts, not a guarantee of the same outcome here, but it's evidence this management/board has a track record of the earlier case not sticking — a data point tempering, not resolving, the current litigation risk.

Research dossier: UBER — Uber Technologies, Inc.

Researched: 2026-07-11 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.55 · Opportunity score: 55

Next earnings: 2026-08-05

Business

A two-sided demand-aggregation marketplace across Mobility (ride-hail), Delivery (Eats/grocery),

and Freight. Uber takes a cut of gross bookings routed through the network; riders/eaters and

drivers/couriers are the two sides, and Uber One (~50M members, >50% of bookings) is the retention

flywheel. Durability rests on the marketplace moat: two-sided liquidity (199M MAPCs, +17% YoY as of

Q1) compounds with scale, and in theory monetizes whoever supplies the ride — including

third-party AV fleets riding on Uber's demand graph. The franchise is structurally FCF-generative

($2.3B FCF in Q1 alone), not a cash-burner.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

Still a buy, but the entry edge is thinner and the central bear risk (AV disintermediation) got a

concrete, negative data point since the last run. Q1 2026 (May 6, still the latest print — Q2

reports Aug 5) was an acceleration quarter: bookings $53.7B (+25% YoY, +21% cc), revenue $13.2B

(+14%), trips 3.64B (+20%), non-GAAP EPS $0.72 (+44%), $3B buyback, Uber One 50M. No new

fundamental print has landed in the two weeks since my prior 06-27 run — the stock is trading

sideways-to-down on sentiment, not new numbers. What did change: on **June 29, Waymo and Uber

ended their robotaxi pilot in Phoenix** — a small deployment (~a dozen vehicles), with Waymo

redirecting those cars to DoorDash delivery and Via transit rather than expanding the Uber

integration. Riders can still reach Waymo directly via the Waymo app. Commentary (The Driverless

Digest) frames this as the "first concrete chip" in Waymo pulling back from the Uber-partnership

model, and flags Austin/Atlanta — Uber's two much larger, exclusive Waymo integrations (hundreds of

vehicles each) — as the names to watch next. Nothing has actually moved in Austin/Atlanta yet, and

Waymo's own July 8 expansion (San Diego, Las Vegas, Tampa, Denver, initially employees-only) is

independent capacity growth, not evidence those markets are going Uber-exclusive or Waymo-direct.

Net: the AV-disintermediation bear case, which was a slow-burn 2028-2030 debate in my prior dive,

now has one small, real, negative data point on the Uber side of the ledger — not a break, but

exactly the kind of thread the falsification section said to watch, and it fired before the next

earnings print.

Micron is one of three global DRAM/NAND makers (with SK Hynix and Samsung), together ~89% of

global DRAM supply. DRAM (server/data-center + increasingly HBM) is the bulk of revenue; NAND

the remainder. Historically the most cyclical semiconductor vertical — oligopoly pricing swings

the P&L violently. The 2025-26 structural change is HBM as a discrete, high-ASP sub-market

driven by GPU training/inference: Micron is #3 in HBM share (~21-24% vs SK Hynix ~43-62%,

Samsung ~17%) but is NVIDIA's swing supplier for HBM4 dual-sourcing, now in volume shipment of

HBM4 for Vera Rubin. Customers have locked ~$22B in take-or-pay long-term supply contracts —

paid regardless of actual offtake, a real change to the demand-visibility picture vs. prior

cycles. Micron is also announcing up to $3B in incremental U.S. investment (concrete poured at

a new NY fab) and holds a GM automotive supply deal plus the 2026-06-22 Anthropic multi-year

HBM/DRAM/SSD supply + co-design agreement (with a direct stake in Anthropic's Series H).

CIENBUYfetched52›

Research dossier: CIEN — Ciena Corporation

Researched: 2026-07-11 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.5 · Opportunity score: 52

Next earnings: 2026-09-03

Business

Ciena designs and sells optical networking hardware, software, and services. The flagship is

WaveLogic coherent optics (the DSP-driven modems that push data down long-haul and data-center

fiber — 800G shipping, 1.6T qualifying), plus packet/routing platforms and a network-management

software layer. The newest product is RLS Hyper-Rail, an intelligent line system co-created

for AI-training interconnect across hundreds of kilometers.

Who pays them: historically Tier-1 carriers (AT&T, Verizon, BT), but growth has fully rotated to

hyperscalers building data-center interconnect (DCI) — the fiber links between AI data

centers carrying petabits/second, plus the DCOM out-of-band management product scaling at Meta

and a second hyperscaler. Ciena is the incumbent leader with proprietary DSP silicon and 20+

years of deployment density. Revenue durability rests on: (a) 7–10-year optical equipment

lifecycles; (b) the operational catastrophe of switching optical vendors mid-build; (c) a

hyperscaler capex wave (~$725B for 2026, +77% YoY) still mid-cycle. This is a substrate bet —

picks-and-shovels paid every time a hyperscaler lights another DCI link

(orchestration-vs-substrate).

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

Closer to yes than the 2026-06-30 read, and for a specific reason: the price has fallen back to

roughly where my own discipline said to buy, and the proximate cause of the fall looks more like

indiscriminate sector beta than a Ciena-specific fundamental problem.

What changed since June 30 ($490.56 → today $460.74, a real ~6% net move but with much larger

intraday swings — screen shows a 52-week high just 27.7% above today's price, meaning CIEN

touched $637 very recently before round-tripping down through the $418–440 range and partially

recovering):

1. June 9 — SemiAnalysis co-packaged-optics (CPO) "delay" report triggered a ~7% CIEN slide

alongside Lumentum (-8%). This report is about switch-side CPO adoption timing — a

technology aimed at intra-rack/switch interconnect, not Ciena's core long-haul/DCI pluggable

business. Ciena is also a participant in the Open CPX MSA (announced March 2026), i.e.

positioned on both sides of the pluggable-vs-CPO debate, not a pure pluggables incumbent

with existential CPO exposure. Read as: the market traded CIEN as a "photonics" beta name on

a headline that bears less directly on its actual product mix than the tape implied. This is

an inference, not a confirmed sourced fact — flagging it as the load-bearing uncertain claim

in this dossier (see Falsification).

2. July 2 — cohort-wide "high-beta AI-infrastructure" reset. CIEN -8.65% same day as

Applied Optoelectronics (-17%), Coherent and Lumentum (-10% each) — explicitly reported as a

valuation-driven sector rotation, not Ciena news. No Ciena-specific 8-K or guidance change

accompanies it.

3. June 11 — $2.875B 0.00% convertible notes due 2031 closed (upsized from $2.0B), initial

conversion price ~$746.66, effective conversion price raised to ~$1,000/share via bond-hedge

+ warrant overlay. Proceeds repaid ~$1.14B of the term loan and repurchased ~0.3M shares.

Net effect: ~$1.7B of net new zero-coupon debt, dilution economically hedged unless the stock

more than doubles from here — a manageable balance-sheet move, not a red flag, but it does

raise gross leverage and is worth tracking into the Sept print.

4. No fundamental update: Q2 print (June 4), $7.7B backlog, FY2026 $6.3B guide, the single

Hyper-Rail multi-rail award (Meta) are all unchanged. No second Hyper-Rail award confirmed.

Net read: this is not "extended without catalyst" (June 30's problem) or "extended with

catalyst" (no new positive fact either) — it's **compressed by cohort beta on a report whose

direct relevance to Ciena's actual business is contestable**, with the balance sheet move being

a second, smaller drag. That is a different, more actionable setup than a melt-up on no news.

Research dossier: RKLB — Rocket Lab Corporation

Researched: 2026-07-07 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.50 · Opportunity score: 52

Next earnings: 2026-08-06

Business

Vertically-integrated space prime — the only credible Western reusable-launch challenger to

SpaceX. Two segments: Launch (Electron, 91+ flights all-time, 12+ in 2026; HASTE suborbital

variant; Neutron, medium-lift reusable, targeting Q4 2026 first flight, five commercial

contracts signed) and Space Systems (satellites, buses, components, solar, separation

systems, flight software — the majority of revenue). Customers pay for rides to orbit

(commercial, civil, increasingly defense — Space Force, SDA, NRO, NASA) and for the hardware

that flies on them. On 2026-06-29 the company agreed to acquire Iridium Communications for

~$8.0B EV ($27 cash + collared stock per Iridium share, collar $67.50–$112.50/RKLB share),

converting the business from a launch/components prime into a vertically-integrated space+satcom

operator with owned L-band spectrum and a 2.55M-subscriber constellation. Expected close

mid-2027.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

**Yes, tentatively — the post-deal air pocket has round-tripped price back into (and now

slightly below) the pre-Iridium entry zone, and the one number everyone was afraid of

(dilution) computes far smaller than the unconfirmed ~33% estimate that was circulating.**

Sequence since the last two dives: RKLB popped +16% to $98.01 on 6/29 (KeyBanc upgrade + the

Iridium announcement), continued to $100.46 by 7/4, then gave essentially all of that back —

$93.37 on 7/6 (-7%, "digesting the deal-driven run-up... rotating out of higher-beta space

stocks," compounded by **CEO Peter Beck filing to sell 5M shares (~$465M, ~0.9% of shares

out)** the day after the deal announcement — a real insider-selling signal, not nothing, though

sized modestly and sourced from 2021 SPAC-merger shares) — and then **$83.41 today (7/7,

-10.4%)**, dragged down with the broader chip/semi complex on the Samsung Q2 revenue-miss

selloff (per state/research/macro.md: SOX -6% to -11% intraday, Micron -4.7%, SK Hynix -9%+).

RKLB's beta (2.55) means it rides the market's AI-demand-scare tape even though satcom/launch

isn't a hyperscaler-capex name — this piece of today's move is market beta, not company news.

Net: the stock is down ~17% from Friday's $100.46 close in three sessions, on a mix of (1)

legitimate profit-taking after an unearned pop, (2) a real but modest insider-sale signal, (3) a

fair analyst debate about post-merger growth mix (blended growth reportedly drops from ~42% to

~22% once Iridium's slower-growing, but profitable, revenue base consolidates — a genuine

re-rating input, not noise), and (4) indiscriminate beta-driven selling in a broad chip scare

unrelated to RKLB's own fundamentals. None of that is a Neutron-execution or Space-Systems

problem — nothing in the underlying launch/backlog story broke this week.

The crux variable from the 7/4 user dive — dilution — I can now bound with real numbers.

Iridium has ~105.7M shares outstanding (10-Q, 2026-03-23). At today's $83.41 (inside the

$67.50–$112.50 collar), the exchange ratio = $27.00 ÷ $83.41 = 0.3237 RKLB shares per Iridium

share → ~34.2M new RKLB shares issued against RKLB's current 578.87M share count — **~5.9%

dilution, not the ~33% figure that was floating around unconfirmed.** (The rest of the $54/share

consideration is cash, funded by the $3.6B bridge loan, not new equity — dilutive to the balance

sheet's leverage, not to share count in the way that was feared.) This is a meaningful, sourced

update against the prior dive's biggest open question, and it points the other way from the

market's apparent fear: single-digit dilution against a profitable, cash-generative asset

(Iridium) is a much better trade than the ~1/3-dilution scenario the stock may have been

half-pricing on the way down. Proxy filing still pending to confirm the exact mechanics, but the

share-count math is arithmetic, not speculation.

Research dossier: MDB — MongoDB, Inc.

Researched: 2026-06-30 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.57 · Opportunity score: 50

Next earnings: 2026-08-27

Business

MongoDB sells a document-oriented database platform. Two revenue buckets:

  • Atlas (cloud-managed, consumption-based) — the growth engine, ~75% of total revenue,

grew 29.4% YoY in Q1 FY2027 and added a record $117M of dollar net-new ARR in one quarter

(four straight quarters of >29% growth). Multi-cloud, serverless, with vector search,

text/time-series search, and stream processing folded in natively — the bet is collapsing a

separate vector store + operational DB + feature store into one managed surface, and becoming

the persistent-state layer for AI agents going to production. (orchestration-vs-substrate:

MDB is an orchestration-side data layer, not GPU substrate — its AI exposure is workload

demand, not the capex J-curve.)

  • Enterprise Advanced + Other (self-managed license + support) — mature, ~+13% YoY,

high-margin, declining share of mix.

Who pays: dev-centric enterprises building modern apps — fintech, e-commerce, gaming, real-time

personalization, AI-agent backends. The document model's schema flexibility fits when data shape

evolves fast (i.e. every AI product in production). Atlas is sticky once pipelines are built on

it. Durability: high.

Last print — Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended 2026-04-30): revenue $687.6M (+25% YoY), an

acceleration from the ~22% trough; non-GAAP op margin 18% (up from 16%); non-GAAP EPS

$1.32 (vs $1.18 est.); a small GAAP net income of +$4.4M (TTM GAAP still −$29M). TTM

revenue $2.60B (+23.6%). No new print since — the next data point is the Aug 27 Q2 report,

so fundamentals are unchanged from the May 28 print.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

**Support held. Catalyst didn't change. So the verdict shouldn't either — it's a hold-of-support

name to accumulate on a real dip, not a buy at $336 with nothing new since May.**

just-cleared hawkish FOMC as the new fact. The open question I left was whether the 200-DMA

Research dossier: NRG — NRG Energy, Inc.

Researched: 2026-07-10 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.55 · Opportunity score: 50

Next earnings: 2026-08-04

Business

NRG is an integrated independent power producer (IPP) + the largest competitive retail

electricity supplier in the US, weighted to Texas/ERCOT and PJM, with a ~25.8 GW generation

fleet after the Jan 30, 2026 close of the ~$12B LS Power acquisition (+13 GW gas/dual-fuel +

the CPower virtual-power-plant platform). Revenue is (1) selling power/retail plans to ~8M+

homes/businesses (sticky, the higher-quality book) and (2) merchant wholesale generation — a

price-taker spread on ERCOT/PJM clearing prices. The growth leg is selling firm power to AI

data centers via the GE Vernova + Kiewit/TIC development agreement (up to ~5.4 GW new gas gen,

1.2 GW by 2029, 1.2 GW by 2030, ~3 GW 2030–32) plus ~445 MW of signed retail data-center

contracts (a 295 MW Texas deal + 150 MW PJM add). This is the AI Energy Thesis expressed

through a large, cash-generative incumbent, but on the grid-connected merchant side —

behind-the-meter gas (Williams–Meta, VoltaGrid, BE) routes around NRG. NRG captures AI load

second-hand, via tighter clearing prices and capacity auction results, not a direct

contracted on-site moat.

Research dossier: CAMT — Camtek Ltd

Researched: 2026-07-11 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.62 · Opportunity score: 47

Next earnings: 2026-08-04 (confirmed — stockanalysis.com)

Business

Camtek is an Israeli semiconductor-equipment company selling inspection and metrology systems

for advanced packaging. Two platforms carry the story: Hawk (3D metrology — bump height,

warpage, co-planarity for HBM and chiplet stacks) and Eagle / Eagle G5 (2D optical

inspection for packaging lines). Customers are OSATs (ASE-, Amkor-type assembly/test houses)

across Asia and the leading HBM makers (Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung-adjacent). Revenue is durable

as long as the HBM/advanced-packaging cycle holds: every AI-accelerator HBM stack needs 3D

inspection and there's no substitute step. FY2025 revenue ~$496M (+16%). Q1 2026 (reported May

12): revenue $121.7M, non-GAAP EPS $0.70, non-GAAP gross margin 51.0%. Q2 2026 guide $129–131M

(+6-7.6% seq); H2 2026 guided >25% above H1 → implied FY run-rate ~$565–570M. Management has

flagged >$260M of 2026–27 revenue already booked from two HBM makers, plus the June 2

disclosed $105M+ order ($55M tier-1 OSAT + $50M+ Hawk from a leading HBM maker, 2027

delivery). Cash-rich balance sheet (~$851M cash per a third-party snapshot). 2026 AGM set for

July 29 (routine director re-election / auditor renewal — no new information expected there).

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

The prior dossier (2026-07-04, $142.50, HOLD/49) flagged two offsetting forces: price falling

further into the buy zone on a cohort selloff, against a newly-quantified negative — SK Hynix

reportedly cutting 2026 HBM4 shipments to Nvidia 20-30% as TrendForce cut Rubin's 2026 GPU-share

forecast from 29% to 22%. A week later, price is essentially unchanged ($142.50 → $143.79 on

7/10, +0.9%; screen shows $144.18) after round-tripping through a $133.26 low on 7/7 (-5.9% that

day, -18.3% on the week at the trough) and partially recovering. No new order, no new guidance,

no fresh CAMT-specific catalyst since the last dive — this was noise around an unchanged

setup, not new information.

**The Rubin/HBM4 story remains genuinely unresolved, and this week's search turned up evidence

pulling in both directions rather than confirming the bear case.** The 20-30% shipment-cut

figure traces to an April 2026 DigiTimes report and is still explicitly unconfirmed by either

Nvidia or SK Hynix — search results this week continue to describe it as "an industry rumor

rather than a finalized decision." Set against that: more recent (June 2026, GTC Taipei)

coverage describes Vera Rubin as now in full production, with Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron

all certified HBM4 suppliers, SK Hynix carrying roughly 60-70% of Rubin HBM4 volume, first

customer shipments this summer, and broad availability targeting H2 2026 — a materially more

bullish cadence than "Rubin ramp delayed, HBM4 redirected to general DRAM." Jensen Huang was

publicly pushing SK Hynix to produce more HBM in early June, the opposite framing from a

capacity-redirection story. These two narratives (April delay rumor vs. June full-production

readout) haven't been reconciled by any single source, and I can't resolve them from search

alone — but the balance of more recent evidence leans toward "ramping now," which is a mild

positive revision from the flatly negative read in last week's dossier.

**A third, independent read (Simply Wall St, 7/9) adds a valuation-discipline flag rather than a

fundamental one**: CAMT's P/E of ~127.7x is "roughly double" the US semiconductor industry

average (~65.3x), and the article characterizes the pullback as "a reassessment of valuation

risk... not a clear buying signal" — a grey-zone read (below analyst targets, above some

intrinsic-value estimates) that argues against treating any dip here as automatically cheap.

This is a useful counterweight to the order-book bull case: the multiple was never priced for a

Rubin-delay outcome, so even a partial resolution toward "ramping as booked" may already be

close to priced in at $144.

Net: with price flat and the Rubin story marginally less bearish on this week's fresher

sources (still unconfirmed either way), the case is essentially unchanged from last week — a

name with real, contracted 2026-27 revenue trading at the low edge of a fair band, gated by an

unresolved supply-chain variable the market hasn't fully priced either direction.

~12× forward earnings / ~10% FCF yield, near its 52-week low, after a ~33–38% YTD drawdown.

Q1 FY27 (reported 2026-05-27) was a clean beat — revenue $11.1B (+13% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $3.88

(+50%), FY27 guide raised to $45.9–46.2B, and a $25B accelerated buyback that puts a real

floor under the share count. Agentforce ARR hit $1.2B (+205% YoY), and 7 of the 10 largest Q1

deals added seats — directly contradicting the disruption narrative. The market is pricing

terminal-value impairment into a business still growing double digits and gushing cash.

The catch: the de-rate is a thesis-narrative dip ("SaaSpocalypse"), not a liquidity dip.

Per macro-cohort-confirmation, cohort-wide weakness driven by information (will AI agents

unresolved. Not a high-conviction at-market buy here.

Research dossier: ESTC — Elastic N.V.

Researched: 2026-06-08 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.55 · Opportunity score: 42

Business

Elastic is an enterprise search, observability, and security platform company built on the ELK stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana). Three pillars: (1) Search — hybrid keyword + vector search, now marketed as "The Search AI Company" powering enterprise RAG applications; (2) Observability — log analytics, APM, infrastructure monitoring; (3) Security — SIEM/XDR. Revenue is >90% subscription, ~80% sales-led. Customers are deeply embedded: the ELK stack is load-bearing infrastructure for search and logging across thousands of enterprises; migration costs are high.

FY2026 full-year revenue: $1.739B (+17% YoY). $100k+ ACV customers: 1,660+. $1M+ ACV customers: >240. Net Expansion Rate: ~112%. AI use cases now penetrate >1/3 of the $100k ACV cohort; AI-using cohorts expand ~5% faster than baseline. AI backlog: >$1B as of Q4 FY26 (May 2026 report).

Why revenue continues: The installed base is structurally sticky (search indices, log pipelines, SIEM rules are not moved lightly). The enterprise-sales motion is converting larger multi-year deals — record $1M+ deal quarter in Q4 FY26, and customers with $5M+ ACV growing ~30% YoY. The platform bet (one vendor for search + observability + security) creates consolidation tailwinds vs. running three point solutions.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

As of June 8, 2026 — 12 days after Q4 FY26 earnings — the answer is: compelling valuation, awkward timing; wait for a cleaner entry.

The business case is genuine:

  • FY27 revenue guidance: $1.985–$2.0B (~15% YoY). Non-GAAP operating margin guided to ~19% (targeting 25% by FY29). FCF margin ~21.5% in FY27 → ~$430M free cash flow on a $6.35B market cap = ~6.8% FCF yield. For a 15% grower with margin expansion, this is dramatically cheap vs. software peers.
  • EV/forward sales: ~2.7x (peer group: Datadog ~10x, CrowdStrike ~18x, MongoDB ~10x). Even applying a steep discount for Elastic's competitive pressures, 3x the current multiple is defensible.
  • AI search positioning is real. Hybrid search (keyword + vector) is the dominant enterprise pattern for RAG applications — Elastic has been doing hybrid search longer than the pure vector DB startups. The $1B+ AI backlog gives near-term revenue visibility.

The timing tension: the Q4 FY26 beat (revenue $451M vs. ~$440M estimate, profitability turn, FY27 guidance) already landed on May 27 and the stock popped +24% from ~$50 to ~$62. That catalyst has been absorbed. The principles mandate: "demand a real dip OR a fresh catalyst." At $62 post-bounce, neither condition is cleanly met. A macro-induced pullback to $52-58 would restore the asymmetry needed to justify a new buy.

Conclusion: fine business, real value, not the right moment to add at $62. HOLD; watch for the re-entry.

Valuation + position vs. range

Price: ~$62 (June 8, 2026)

52-week range: $42.05 – $96.07

Position: 45% above the 52-week low; 36% below the 52-week high — squarely in the middle of the range, post-bounce.

Market cap: ~$6.35B

How much is already priced in: the FY26 beat and FY27 guidance raise are in the price. The AI backlog converting to consumption revenue acceleration — if it materializes in FY27 earnings prints — is not fully in the price yet.

Post-deal / repriced check

ESTC is not a Wait-for-deal thesis name. It's an established public company with no pending hyperscaler partnership the market is waiting on. The relevant repricing event here was the Q4 FY26 earnings catalyst (May 27, 2026): revenue beat, profitability turn, FY27 guidance, AI backlog disclosure. That landed 12 days ago and the +24% jump is in the price.

This is analogous to a post-deal scenario in the sense that the most recent catalyst has been absorbed. The old low-price entry opportunity ($42-50 pre-earnings) is gone. The question from here is whether the post-catalyst multiple (3.65x P/S, ~$62) is worth owning. It is — but only marginally at today's price vs. a better entry 10% lower.

There is no pending deal or partnership announcement that changes this calculus on a binary basis.

Council (one line each, no hedging)

  • Bull: At 2.7x EV/forward revenue with a 6.8% FCF yield and $1B AI backlog, Elastic is priced like a dying business while actually compounding at 15% with expanding margins — the discount is explained by competitive narrative, not business reality.
  • Bear: AWS OpenSearch permanently impaired the open-source moat, Datadog owns observability mindshare, CrowdStrike/Splunk own enterprise SIEM, and 15% growth at decelerating trend is the ceiling, not the floor — re-rating never comes.
  • First-principles: A business generating $430M in annual FCF from $2B in enterprise revenue, growing at 15% with sticky installed base and hybrid-search AI positioning, should trade at more than $6.35B; at the current price you are buying real cash flows cheaply, not speculating on a thesis.

  • Stretch: $102 — 5x+ forward; requires AI backlog conversion to produce revenue acceleration in FY27 Q1-Q2 prints above the ~15% baseline guidance

Current price at ~$62 is above my buy-below ($58). Not a buy today; re-enter on the dip.

Kill-switches: All three clear (see state/research/macro.md). Hyperscaler capex still accelerating at +67-77% YoY benefits Elastic's observability business (more compute = more logs, metrics, traces) and validates AI search demand. No kill-switch concern.

Rate constraint: With cuts pushed to September/October 2026 at earliest, multiple-expansion is on hold for high-P/S names. The FCF yield of 6.8% provides a real rate-of-return anchor.

Regime: Extended market, narrow breadth, CAPE at 42x. A broad market correction of 10-15% (possible if June FOMC or May CPI hawkish) would take ESTC to $52-55 — roughly my buy-below target, incidentally. Not a reason to panic if already held; is a reason to wait before adding at $62.

Research dossier: GEV — GE Vernova

Researched: 2026-06-09 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.60 · Opportunity score: 42

Business

GE Vernova (spun from GE, April 2024) is the energy-technology company with three segments:

1. Power (~$23B revenue) — gas turbines, aeroderivatives, nuclear steam, gas engines. The sold-out core. Gas turbine slot reservations have grown from 83 → 100 GW through Q1 2026, targeting 110 GW by year-end. New equipment pricing running 10–20% above Q4 2025 levels in a seller's market.

2. Electrification (~$13.9B projected 2026, +44% YoY) — grid transformers, switchgear, HVDC systems, software. Data-center-driven demand is the growth engine: $2.4B in data-center equipment orders in Q1 2026 alone, more than all of 2025 combined. Book-to-bill ~2.5x.

3. Wind (~$7B) — offshore and onshore wind; still margin-challenged but improving. Not the thesis driver; margin drag remains.

Who pays them: utilities, hyperscalers, independent power producers, grid operators globally. Power and Electrification revenue is long-cycle (backlog → execution over 3–5 years). Services contracts on installed base provide a durable recurring stream once gas turbines are shipped.

Why it continues: hyperscaler AI buildout is inelastic to GEV's pricing; the grid-upgrade backlog for HVDC and transformers is multi-year regardless of macro. GEV's only scaled competition in gas turbines is Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi — no new entrant can build that manufacturing capacity in years.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

The AI energy thesis is as directly applicable here as anywhere in the field. Power IS the binding constraint, and GEV is the picks-and-shovels supplier. Q1 2026 results confirmed the thesis is accelerating, not decelerating:

  • Orders +71% organic to $18.3B — not a one-quarter fluke; driven by both gas turbine reservations and electrification
  • Backlog at record $163B (+$13B sequential), now targeting $200B by 2027 (one year ahead of prior plan)
  • Gas turbine slots filling through 2030: pricing power is locked in for years, not quarters
  • Guidance raised to $44.5–45.5B revenue / 12–14% adj. EBITDA / $6.5–7.5B FCF for 2026

The question isn't whether GEV is a great business — it demonstrably is. The question is whether $939 is a good entry. The stock has already run from ~$458 a year ago to a high of $1,182, then pulled back 21% to $939. In an extended market with 3.8% CPI and no rate cuts until fall 2026 at earliest, the current pullback reflects macro multiple compression rather than fundamental deterioration. That's encouraging for the business but doesn't resolve the valuation question: at ~37x 2026 FCF, you are paying for the continued strong execution of an already-proven story.

Verdict: HOLD. The business is excellent, the pullback from peak is real (21%), but the price is at/near fair value for THIS macro environment. I'm not finding a genuine margin of safety at $939.

Valuation + position vs. range

My own fair-value derivation:

Using FCF multiple for a high-quality industrial with pricing power and backlog visibility:

  • 30x 2026 FCF ($7B) = $210B market cap → $778/share (deep-value entry, demanding a discount)
  • 35x 2026 FCF = $245B → $907/share (fair; captures pricing power + backlog premium)
  • 40x 2026 FCF = $280B → $1,037/share (stretch; requires rate cuts to justify)
  • 45x 2026 FCF = $315B → $1,167/share (analyst consensus range; priced for perfection)

At $939, the stock trades at ~37x 2026 FCF — between my fair (~$907) and stretch (~$1,037) bands. Not cheap; not obviously broken.

Using 2027 FCF (if growth trajectory continues to ~$9–10B), the picture looks better: 25–28x — more defensible for a business of this quality. But that requires continued execution through an uncertain macro.

Post-deal / repriced check

GEV is post-IPO (April 2024) and post-multiple-re-rate. The stock was in the $100s at spin; the AI-energy thesis became widely appreciated through 2025 and the stock ran accordingly. At $939, this is not a "pre-deal" entry. The 21% pullback from the $1,182 peak is meaningful, but the 52-week run of +105% makes clear the entry-edge from the pre-recognition phase has been consumed.

The extended-with-vs-without-catalyst check: the Q1 2026 blowout (April 22) is a FRESH thesis-confirming catalyst — orders +71%, backlog record, guidance raised. The stock's decline from $1,182 to $939 POST that catalyst is instructive: either the market disagrees with the valuation even after the blowout, or the macro environment (3.8% CPI, rate compression) is capping the multiple. Both suggest the repricing is not done. The old entry edge is gone; to enter here requires building a new entry case from the current data, which yields a fair-value range of $907–$1,037 — straddling current price.

Council (one line each, no hedging)

  • Bull: $163B backlog + 100 GW turbine slots locked through 2030 + pricing running 10–20% above prior levels = a multi-year compounding machine the market is temporarily discounting on macro noise.
  • Bear: At 37x 2026 FCF in a rising-rate, no-cut environment, the multiple has nowhere to go but down until the Fed actually moves, and the Wind segment is still a margin anchor.
  • First-principles: A business with locked-in demand, pricing power, and irreplaceable manufacturing capacity trading at 37x FCF is priced for continued excellence — it's not expensive enough to avoid, but not cheap enough to chase in a market with 3.8% CPI and CAPE of 42x.

Regime: Extended. S&P trailing P/E 25.3x, CAPE 42.3x, Buffett Indicator 237%. CPI at 3.8% with no cuts expected until fall 2026 at earliest. Opportunity-cost rank: Compared to the field:

Business

Rambus sells memory interface chips — the DDR5 server-DIMM chipset (Registering Clock

Drivers / RCDs, companion data-buffer chips, PMICs, temp sensors) that sits between the CPU and

DRAM modules — plus silicon IP (security IP, interface IP licensed into SoCs) and a legacy

patent-licensing royalty stream. Customers are DIMM module makers and server/hyperscaler

OEMs; they pay because every DDR5 server module needs an RCD, and Rambus holds >40% RCD share

(WebSearch, servethehome-style trade coverage). Revenue is per-module silicon content: as the

industry steps DDR5 → MRDIMM (each MRDIMM-12800 needs 1 MRCD + 10 MDB chips) and adds new

formats (LPDDR5X SOCAMM2 for AI server platforms, announced 2026-04-22), dollar content per

module rises even at flat unit volumes. Rambus was also first to launch HBM4 PHY + controller

IP, positioning it as a gatekeeper AI-accelerator vendors are hard to route around. Management's

own framing on the Q1 2026 call: MRDIMM initial volume starts late 2026 on Intel/AMD platform

launches, the real ramp is a 2027 story, and the ~$600M MRDIMM TAM isn't realized until 2028;

SOCAMM2's 2026 revenue impact is explicitly negligible. The AI-memory-bandwidth build is a real

secular tailwind — it's a 2027-28 P&L event, not a 2026 one.

Research dossier: LRCX — Lam Research Corporation

Researched: 2026-07-11 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.55 · Opportunity score: 40

Next earnings: 2026-07-29

Business

Lam Research is one of the three dominant wafer-fabrication-equipment (WFE) makers, alongside

Applied Materials and Tokyo Electron. Its franchise is etch and deposition — the tools that

carve and layer 3D structures in leading-edge logic and especially 3D NAND, where Lam is

share leader. Customers are the chipmakers (TSMC, Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, Intel). This sits

one layer below the AI picks-and-shovels layer: hyperscaler capex pulls HBM/leading-edge logic

demand, which pulls fab buildout, which pulls Lam's etch/dep tools plus a large recurring

service/spares ("CSBG") tail on the installed base. Revenue durably continues because every

node transition and new fab is more etch/dep-intensive, and the installed base throws off

high-margin service regardless of the equipment cycle. Nothing about this business logic has

changed since the last dive.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

Since the last dossier (2026-06-11, $362.52, HOLD), LRCX ran further to a fresh **all-time high

of $438.50 before getting caught in a cohort-wide semicap de-rating on July 2-3**: SOX fell

as much as 6% intraday (worst two-day semi decline in a month), KLA -12%, Teradyne -14%,

Applied Materials -7 to -10%, Axcelis -19%, and LRCX itself down ~9.7-10.2% on July 2 alone

(TradingKey,

QuiverQuant).

This was not an LRCX-specific event — drivers were sector-wide: a report Meta plans to

resell excess data-center capacity (an unwelcome "overcapacity" signal for the whole AI-capex

cohort), lingering digestion of Broadcom's June print that didn't deliver the AI-guidance

upgrade the market wanted, and renewed SK Hynix HBM-capacity-expansion caution — a

valuation/rotation shakeout riding on top of a name that had doubled in H1 2026, not a

change in Lam's own fundamentals. Since the pullback, price has gone essentially sideways

($351.41 close July 2 → $350.33 today) — no bounce yet, but no further breakdown either.

CEO Timothy Archer filed a Form 144 to sell 30,000 shares, alongside a $19.1M sale by a

director and $4.6M by an SVP. This lines up with the CEO's standing Rule 10b5-1 plan (adopted

Aug 19 2025, expired May 29 2026, likely renewed) and a Dec-2025 10b5-1 sale of similar shape —

a routine executive-liquidity pattern, not a fresh signal (the FSLR dive on 2026-07-07 found the

same 10b5-1 shape for that name's CEO and concluded routine, not front-running). Read this as a

mild watch item, not a red flag.

Research dossier: NET — Cloudflare, Inc.

Researched: 2026-06-20 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.62 · Opportunity score: 40

Next earnings: 2026-07-30

Business

Cloudflare runs a global connectivity cloud — 320+ points of presence carrying CDN, DDoS

mitigation, zero-trust/SASE access, and edge developer compute (Workers). Revenue is

subscription-led with heavy usage-based upsell: ~78% gross margins, ~120% net dollar retention,

and an enterprise cohort that compounds (deals >$1M up 73% YoY in Q1, record adds at the >$5M

tier). The network is a utility for a meaningful slice of internet traffic and the zero-trust

stack creates sticky multi-year enterprise contracts — that's the durable base.

The growth bet layered on top is repositioning the network as AI-agent infrastructure:

Workers AI (edge GPU inference), AI Gateway (LLM traffic routing/caching), and the May 19 2026

Cloudflare Environments for Claude Managed Agents partnership with Anthropic (run enterprise

Claude agents on Cloudflare's network with zero-trust + global latency). Agents Week (June 2026)

ran 241B tokens through Workers AI; the June 4 VoidZero acquisition folds Vite/Vitest/Rolldown

dev tooling into one-click edge deploy. Real products with real usage — but not yet a visible

revenue line.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

The setup has improved since the 2026-06-09 dossier (HOLD at ~$248) — but not enough to flip.

The stock crashed 24% to ~$194 on the May 7 Q1 print (a clean beat — rev $639.8M +34%,

non-GAAP EPS $0.25 vs $0.23 — overshadowed by the first mass layoff in company history, 1,100

roles / 20% of staff, framed by Prince as "AI made these jobs obsolete"). It then rebounded

(+11% June 1, +3.6% June 11 to $227) and has since drifted back to ~$224. So today's price is a

~10% pullback off the early-June recovery high, sitting in my fair-value zone.

What's genuinely good here: the AI-agent positioning is product, not slideware (Anthropic

runtime + 241B tokens of real traffic), the enterprise expansion engine is intact (120% NRR,

$1M deals +73%), and the layoff — read past the alarming framing — is a margin lever: $140-150M

of one-time charges that should step run-rate FCF up from ~13%. NET's own dip-buyer base rate is

favorable (44 prior instances: 55%/59%/68% win at +21/+42/+63d, avg +16% at +63d), which says

buying this name in this kind of pullback has historically paid.

What stops me from buying at $224: (1) it's ~28× forward P/S — a high-duration SaaS multiple in

a regime explicitly hostile to duration (no 2026 cuts, hike tail); (2) there is **no fresh

catalyst** since June 9 — this is a quiet drift lower, partly cohort de-rating, not a

thesis-confirming-catalyst dip the macro stance demands; (3) the load-bearing question —

does the AI-agent platform show up in the top line? — isn't answerable until July 30; (4) the

layoff carries a real bear read (is Cloudflare hedging against AI compressing its own demand?).

The dip-buyer edge is real but doesn't override paying above fair value with the proof point six

weeks out.

Bottom line: Excellent business, improving entry, favorable base rate — but priced just above

my fair value, no new catalyst, and the monetization tell lands July 30. Hold; let a deeper dip

or the print be the trigger.

Valuation + position vs. range

At ~28× forward sales the market is paying the quality-and-NDR premium plus a down-payment on

Post-deal / repriced check

Not a Wait-for-deal thesis name in the GPU/energy sense — there's no single lab-partnership

VoidZero (June 4) and Agents Week are all 2–6 weeks old and already in the tape (the stock made

its run, crashed on earnings, recovered). Buying $224 today is not buying ahead of those

catalysts — it's buying after them, on a drift, before the revenue proof. Per the framework, an

old (even if good) catalyst is not an entry case.

runtime — if agent traffic becomes the next usage layer, NET monetizes it from a sticky 120%-NRR

Researched: 2026-06-19 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.6 · Opportunity score: 40

Business

The world's dominant pure-play foundry — it manufactures the leading-edge logic (and increasingly the advanced packaging) that everyone else designs. Customers are the fabless ecosystem: NVIDIA, Apple, AMD, Broadcom, Qualcomm. Revenue durably continues because TSM is a near-monopoly at the leading edge (3nm/2nm) and the binding bottleneck of the AI buildout. This is the "wafers" half of Gavin Baker's "watts and wafers" — and per Nvidia - AI Cycle Durability and GPU Economics, TSM's restraint (disciplined capacity adds run by "flinty old-school veterans") is what smooths and elongates the cycle by preventing an overbuild. Wafer intensity may be AI's savior; TSM is the toll booth.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

The business is firing on all cylinders, but the entry is the question, and at ~$462 (0.6% off the 52-week high, +34.6% over 60d, +37.9% above the 200DMA) this is an extended chart. Q1 2026 (reported Apr 16): revenue $35.9B (+6.4% QoQ USD), gross margin 66.2% (record, beat the high guide by 120bp), operating margin 58.1%, HPC 61% of revenue (+20% QoQ). They raised full-year 2026 revenue-growth guidance to above 30% in USD and guided Q2 to $39.0–40.2B (+10% QoQ) at 65.5–67.5% GM. June 4 annual meeting: CoWoS advanced-packaging is sold out through 2026, lead times to ~104 weeks, capacity meeting only ~80% of demand (NVDA ~60% of it). All genuinely bullish — but all of it is already in the price: the print is two months old and the CoWoS commentary is incremental, not a step-change. Per extended-with-vs-without-catalyst, the operative test is "what business fact changed in the last 7–14 days?" — nothing material did. So the run is continuation/momentum, not fresh repricing. Extended without a fresh catalyst → don't chase here.

Valuation + position vs. range

  • Price $462.12 (Jun 18), market cap $1.98T, TTM revenue $128.3B, net margin 46.5%.
  • Trailing P/E ~33, forward P/E ~23, P/S 15.4 (stockanalysis.com, fetched). Up +116% over the trailing 52 weeks.
  • The forward P/E of ~23 against >30% revenue growth, 66% gross margin and 46% net margin is not egregious on quality — PEG well under 1 and roughly in line with the broad market's ~22.5× forward P/E despite far better economics. The stretch is positional, not multiple-based: it sits at the very top of its range after a vertical run. P/S 15.4 is the number that bites if the market de-rates.

Post-deal / repriced check

Wait-for-deal thesis doesn't apply cleanly — TSM isn't a small/mid pre-deal infra name awaiting a lab partnership; it's the structural substrate, a durable compounder, not a windowed supply/demand trade. But the spirit of the check does: the bull facts (record margins, raised guide, CoWoS sold out) are consumed by the +116% repricing. "It was a great business at $300" is true and irrelevant to whether $462 at the 52-week high is an entry. The old bull case is not an entry case here.

Council (one line each, no hedging)

  • Bull: The single most defensible toll booth in AI — wafers and CoWoS are the bottleneck, sold out through 2026 at 104-week lead times, and a forward P/E of 23 underprices >30% growth at 66% gross margin.

Bitdeer Technologies Group (NASDAQ: BTDR) is a Bitcoin miner executing a funded pivot into AI/HPC data-center infrastructure. Founded by Jihan Wu (Bitmain co-founder). Three revenue legs: (1) self-mining BTC — still the dominant engine (70.2 EH/s self-mining hashrate, 83.1 EH/s under management as of May 2026); (2) mining hosting / cloud hashrate; (3) AI Cloud — early GPU colocation + cloud (ARR ~$69M at 90% utilization, 4,248 GPUs deployed). It designs its own ASICs (SEALMINER line; A4 at 9.45 J/T, plus the DL1 Hydro Scrypt rig) for internal use and sale — the in-house silicon is a genuine cost edge over miners buying third-party rigs.

The durable differentiator is power-advantaged sites inside a stated ~3GW global power portfolio: Norway (Tydal — Phase 1 50MW + Phase 2 175MW, hydro, Nvidia Vera Rubin reference design, both phases now targeted for Q4-2026 energization) and a 570MW Clarington, Ohio site (power under contract with AEP). Management has explicitly reframed the story: colocation, not BTC appreciation, is the compounding bet, and "executing colocation lease agreements" is named top priority.

Why AI-colocation revenue would durably continue: cheap Norwegian hydro + EU data-sovereignty pull create real demand for EU-based AI compute. The open question is unchanged across three dives now — the anchor customer is still unsigned, so pricing power and customer quality remain unconfirmed.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

**Still pre-customer, and the net of the last 7 days is mixed-to-slightly-negative. This is a textbook Wait-for-deal thesis structure: power-rich, Nvidia-aligned sites ahead of a signed hyperscaler/AI-lab anchor. If a named customer signs the Tydal lease this reprices hard (the BE-post-Oracle "sustained repricing" pattern is the analog). Applying extended-with-vs-without-catalyst's operational test — what fact about the business changed in the last 7–14 days? — the honest answer:

  • Tydal: still "advanced negotiations," no signature. The language is now a month stale; protracted negotiation without close is a mild yellow flag, not a catalyst.
  • Clarington (NEW, negative): the 570MW Ohio site is delayed by legal proceedings filed by a neighboring company (American Heavy Plate Solutions LLC); no energization timeline given. This narrows the near-term colocation surface to Tydal alone.
  • Production: 921 BTC mined in May (+370% YoY), record hashrate — strong operational color, but mining is the gross-margin-negative leg, so volume isn't the value driver.

Business

Marvell designs data-center semiconductors around two load-bearing franchises: **custom

ASICs/XPUs** for hyperscalers (Amazon Trainium, Microsoft Maia, Meta's new DPU, plus a Google

Axion/TPU-adjacent engagement) and networking/interconnect silicon (Ethernet switch ASICs,

optical DSPs, SerDes, and — after the Celestial AI and XConn acquisitions — silicon photonics).

Data center is ~76% of revenue and is essentially the entire growth story, alongside a formal

NVIDIA tie via NVLink Fusion (~$2B NVIDIA investment, Mar 2026). Management's design-win

pipeline is now framed at ~$75B in lifetime revenue across 18 secured XPU/XPU-attach sockets

(several in volume production) plus 50+ active custom-AI engagements across 10+ customers,

targeting $10B of FY2029 revenue from those programs specifically. Revenue durability rests on

3-5-year custom-silicon design cycles (once a hyperscaler tapes out with Marvell IP embedded,

mid-generation switching is near-impossible) plus an interconnect/SerDes/photonics IP moat

beneath any single chip generation — the same orchestration-vs-substrate logic as Broadcom,

at a structurally weaker market position: Broadcom holds an estimated ~60% share of hyperscaler

custom-ASIC design wins; Marvell is the #2 challenger, more customer-concentrated (45% of

revenue through a single distributor, 82% from the top 10 customers per this run's search) —

real revenue, but "lumpier" than Broadcom's book, and one program delay away from a sharper

re-rate.

CLSK-2026-07-14-signed-lease-buy›

CLSK — BUY memo — 2026-07-14

Decision

BUY $10.00 CLSK @ ~$13.05 (order filled ~$12.99, 0.769820 sh), 14:05 UTC.

Signal: 2026-07-14:CLSK:price:gap+move+vol. Confidence: 0.6. Order id 6a56420c-eccf-4832-8032-d59286f2aa34 (ref_id 35d89689-669f-5356-9846-76d9510a2c51).

Reasoning

The 2026-06-23 dossier (HOLD/0.6/opp 38) explicitly flagged the Sandersville lease as the

falsification trigger: "Meta lease signs (IG counterparty, MW, term, ≥~$200/kW/mo economics) →

flips toward BUY even paid-up." Today's PRNewswire release (06:00 ET, 8-K confirmed) is exactly

that: a signed 20-year lease (two 5-year extensions), 175MW critical IT load, Sandersville GA,

~$6.6B contracted revenue over the initial term (~$11.6B with extensions), ~$330M/yr average NOI,

with a high-investment-grade unnamed global tech counterparty — plus a new LOI covering CleanSpark's

entire Texas portfolio (718 acres, up to 885MW). This is a definitive signed deal, not the

negotiation-stage Meta rumor the dossier was pricing.

Crucially, price at decision time ($13.05, drifting to ~$12.99 fill) sits AT the dossier's own

buy-below level (~$13, the 200DMA) — not in the $17-18 "stretch/chase-only" band the dossier

reserved for a signed deal. The stock has round-tripped down from $17.19 (dossier date) to

pre-gap $12.36 close, so the confirmed catalyst is landing at a genuine dip level, not an

extension. Per extended-with-vs-without-catalyst, paying up is justified when a fresh

thesis-confirming catalyst just landed — here it landed exactly at the buy-below price, the

strongest version of that setup.

Macro gate: regime is "hold cash, demand a real dip or fresh catalyst" (hawkish Fed, CAPE

stretched, no kill-switches tripped). This trade satisfies both prongs at once — real price

level + fresh catalyst — which is why it clears the bar despite the broader hold-cash stance.

Opportunity-cost: the board rank (#55/127, opp 38) is stale — computed pre-catalyst. The

dossier's own 90-day falsification path said a second-site/multi-tenant HPC commitment (which

today's Texas LOI partially delivers alongside the signed Sandersville lease) would push opp

score to 65-70+. No held position was rotated to fund this — sized from available cash

($11.59) at a $10 starter, leaving the book intact.

Entry shape

Bought at market in regular hours (fractional, $10 notional) — no timing edge to invent

intraday; acting on the pre-planned buy-below level now that the catalyst confirmed at that

price simultaneously.

What would change my mind

Registered as expectations (see below):

1. Counterparty identity confirmed as the previously-reported Meta, or another named IG

hyperscaler, by 2026-08-06 (Q3 FY26 earnings) — strengthens conviction, doesn't gate the

entry (already acted on the lease terms alone).

2. Q3 FY2026 print (~2026-08-06): hashrate/BTC production holding AND progress on the Texas

LOI converting to a definitive agreement — thesis-confirming path to the $22-24 prior-high

band.

3. Deal walk-back / counterparty dispute / lease termination before 2026-09-14 — would flip

this from confirmed-catalyst re-rate back to unsigned-rumor pricing, thesis broken.

Note to future self

Mirrored via --note: watch Q3 FY26 print (2026-08-06) for hosting-revenue contract detail and

Texas LOI progression; watch for counterparty naming.

RKLB-2026-07-14-trigger-hold-bounce-consumed›

RKLB — 2026-07-14 — HOLD (trigger:buy:77 signal, contradicts dossier BUY)

Decision

HOLD. Signal 2026-07-14:RKLB:trigger:buy:77 (trigger, sev 3, level 77, struck $76.77 at

13:00:47 UTC). Position held: 0.02944 sh, avg cost $84.93, entered 2026-07-08. Confidence 0.55.

Time ~13:50 UTC 2026-07-14. No order placed.

Reasoning

The dossier (struck 2026-07-07 @ $83.41) rates RKLB BUY with a $85 buy-below / $83-86 fair band,

and this trigger fired on a further dip to $76.77 — arithmetically still inside "buy" territory

by the dossier's own levels. But by the time this run reconciled the broker and pulled a live

quote, price had already bounced to $81.46 — a +6.1% move in the ~45 minutes since the signal

fired, with nothing in the bundle (no news, no macro shift) explaining it. Per the re-rate-on-

drift discipline, a BUY sized off a dip price is not still a BUY after an unexplained bounce

consumes the edge — this is the same "extended-with-vs-without-catalyst" trap that correctly

produced HOLD on 2026-07-09 when RKLB bounced off its $85 falsification level with no catalyst.

Separately, and independent of the drift: this would be an ADD to an existing position (entered

6d ago, still -4.1% vs cost), and the opportunity-cost gate doesn't clear. Cash is $11.59 of

$100. RKLB ranks #23/127 (opp 52) — NVDA (62), GOOGL (60), and SNPS (60) are all unheld and

rank higher. Committing the last of the cash to add to an already-held, rank-#23 name while

better-ranked names sit unheld and unbought is exactly the failure the opportunity-cost lens

guards against.

Also weighing: this exact ticker has thrashed BUY→HOLD→BUY→HOLD three times in the last six

days (7/8→7/9→7/9-7/10 BUY period→7/13 HOLD), and the calibration ledger marks those switches

at -2.5%, -6.0%, and -9.3% respectively. Flipping again on a bare 45-minute bounce, without a

new fact or a better method, would repeat the pattern rather than correct it.

Entry shape

Deferred-with-trigger, not permanent pass. The dossier's underlying case (post-Iridium

mispricing, ~5.9% dilution not ~33%) is unchanged and still open — the disqualifier here is

purely today's price action and the cash/rank gate, not a thesis break. If (a) price gives back

today's bounce and holds ≤$79-80 into the close with no negative catalyst, or (b) cash frees up

via a rotation that a future run can defend on its own terms (not funded by RKLB churn), revisit

sizing a further add then.

What would change my mind

1. RKLB regular-session close back at/below ~$79-80 today with no fresh negative catalyst —

reopens the case that the dip, not the bounce, is the real price.

2. NVDA/GOOGL/SNPS get bought first, or a rotation frees cash specifically evaluated as better

spent on RKLB than on those names — only then does an add clear opportunity-cost.

3. Iridium proxy filing (no fixed date) confirming or correcting the ~5.9% dilution estimate —

still the standing structural falsifier from the 7/8 entry memo, unresolved.

Note to future self

Mirrored via --note below: don't add to RKLB off a bare intraday bounce/dip pair — either

wait for a genuine catalyst or for NVDA/GOOGL/SNPS to get funded first (rank gate), and stop

re-litigating this name's price noise without new information.

DGXX-2026-07-14-research-verdict-opp-cost-hold›

DGXX — HOLD (research_verdict converted to a considered pass)

Decision

Action: HOLD. Signal: 2026-07-13:DGXX:research:buy (research_verdict, sev 4).

Time: 2026-07-14T13:30Z (pre-market, ~2 min before regular open). Confidence: 0.4.

Reference price: $4.42 (last pre-market trade; bid $4.40 / ask $4.47), vs. yesterday's $4.25 close.

Reasoning

The agent's own dossier (2026-07-13, BUY/0.35/opp 32) is real and well-argued: 0.35x

price-to-backlog against a funded Cerebras counterparty, a third consecutive confirmed

cohort-red day, no fresh negative DGXX news. But two things fail this specific conversion

from research to entry:

1. Opportunity-cost gate fails. DGXX ranks #75/127 (opp 32) on today's board. Cash is

$11.59 of a $97.60 book, and every dollar of that is competing against BUY-rated names

already IN the book at meaningfully higher rank: FN (#1, opp 71), NVT (#3, opp 61), CEG

(#4, opp 60), FSLR (#11, opp 55), SNDK (#13, opp 55), RKLB (#23, opp 52), POWL (#22, opp

52). A lottery-sized DGXX starter would not be the best use of the marginal dollar — it

would be reaching past six higher-ranked BUYs already held. This isn't "little cash forces

HOLD" reflexively; it's that the ranked alternatives are concretely better, which is exactly

what the opportunity-cost lens is for.

2. Price has already run past the dossier's own entry gate, pre-catalyst. The dossier's

buy-below is $4.30, struck off yesterday's $4.25 close. Pre-market this morning DGXX is

quoting $4.40/$4.47 (last trade $4.42) — already ~4% above that gate with zero incremental

news (still no Pleasants update, no fresh cohort move overnight beyond the same BTC/Iran

backdrop already priced in). Per Price levels: inputs, not laws, buying above the entry

level without a genuinely new catalyst is the IREN-at-$61 mistake in miniature. This reads

as the tail of yesterday's cohort bounce, not a fresh signal.

Both cut the same direction, so this is a considered HOLD, not a reflexive one — the dossier's

thesis stands, but neither the price nor the rank supports converting it to an entry today.

Entry shape

Not buying now. If both conditions clear — price back at/under ~$4.30 at a confirmed regular-

session print, AND DGXX's opportunity rank moves up past the lowest-ranked currently-held BUY

— the lottery-starter case (1-2% of book, capped) reopens. No timing edge otherwise; this is a

level-and-rank gate, not an intraday call.

What would change my mind

  • DGXX regular-session price prints back at/below $4.30 with the cohort-confirmation read still

intact (not DGXX-specific bad news).

  • A rank improvement that puts DGXX above at least one currently-held BUY for the marginal

dollar.

  • Any Pleasants Power Station news (the open thread) — would re-rate the optionality leg either

direction.

Note to future self

Mirrored via --note: watch for DGXX back at/under $4.30 confirmed at regular-session open, or

a rank move above the lowest-ranked held BUY, before reconsidering the lottery starter.

Decision

HOLD, $0, entry_price $658.21 (live quote). 2026-07-13 ~14:45 UTC. Signal 2026-07-11:META:research:buy. Confidence 0.55.

Reasoning

fresh catalysts: Meta Compute cloud-business reporting, shipped competitive models (Muse

Spark/Image), a credible SemiAnalysis report card, and a capex raise to $125-145B. All three

kill-switches clean; nothing here is FOMO-on-a-chart.

But the dossier itself flags that the tradeable dip it bought on 6/27 (~$550) is gone — price

is up 21.7% in ten sessions to $669, now trading ~3% above its own re-derived buy-below ($650),

with fair value re-rated up to ~$795. Per extended-with-vs-without-catalyst: the catalyst cluster

justifies a fair-value re-rate, but two of the three legs (Meta Compute, capex reaction) are

still unmonetized/unconfirmed — paying up past the buy-below chases the rumor, doesn't buy the

landed fact.

Opportunity-cost: cross-rank is #18/126 (opp 52), mid-pack — the dossier's own read calls it

"good, not standout." FN (#1, opp 71), NVT (#3, 61), CEG (#4, 60), FSLR (#10, 55) are all

currently HELD and out-rank META for the marginal dollar. Buying power is $1.59 today (cash

$11.59 mostly tied up in the in-flight AMZN->MU rotation, settlement due 2026-07-14) — no real

position is fundable regardless of the rank call, so forcing a rotation out of a lower-ranked

holding (WULF/CAMT/APLD) into a name that isn't even at its own entry level would be compounding

one in-flight rotation with a second, weaker one.

Micro-council:

  • Bull: AI lab just proved it can ship competitive models and floated a second revenue line,

still below a conservatively re-derived fair value.

  • Bear: chasing a 21%-in-2wk move into a July 29 print where guidance (not the beat) decides the

reaction, pricing an unlaunched cloud business that has no date, pricing, or customer.

  • First-principles: even stripped of AI optionality the ad business alone isn't expensive at

~19x forward — but the premium being paid today is exactly the part that unwinds fastest if

Meta Compute details disappoint.

Entry shape

Not buying at market above the dossier's own buy-below with no fresh (post-7/10) catalyst.

Waiting for either (a) a pullback to $650 (buy-below) or $600-620 (strong-add, re-opens the wider

discount), or (b) a confirmed Meta Compute launch (product/pricing/named customer) — that's the

"deal lands" moment this dossier explicitly treats as the next real look. No timing edge beyond

the pre-derived levels; not inventing intraday precision.

Registered on the expectations ledger:

1. Meta Compute launches with confirmed product, pricing, and a named customer by 2026-08-15 —

3. Q2 print (2026-07-29): ad-revenue growth holds ~20-30% AND no walk-back on Meta Compute during

the call — a walk-back would be the clearest near-term falsifier of this week's rally.
